title: Network Security Groups and Azure Firewall
description: Secure Azure network traffic with NSGs and Azure Firewall.

data.text: Your multi-tier app needs: web tier accessible from internet, app tier only from web tier, database only from app tier. Outbound traffic must be logged and restricted to approved endpoints. Which Azure security controls do you use?
Use **NSGs** on subnets for tier-to-tier access control. Use **Azure Firewall** for centralized outbound control, FQDN filtering, and full logging. Enable **Azure DDoS Protection** for the VNet.

data.title: Azure CLI - NSG Rules for Multi-Tier
data.code:
# Web -> App (port 8080)
az network nsg rule create \
  --nsg-name 'nsg-app' \
  --resource-group 'rg-network' \
  --name 'Allow-Web-to-App' \
  --priority 100 \
  --direction Inbound \
  --access Allow \
  --protocol Tcp \
  --source-address-prefixes 10.0.1.0/24 \
  --source-port-ranges '*' \
  --destination-address-prefixes 10.0.2.0/24 \
  --destination-port-ranges 8080

# App -> DB (port 1433)
az network nsg rule create \
  --nsg-name 'nsg-data' \
  --resource-group 'rg-network' \
  --name 'Allow-App-to-DB' \
  --priority 100 \
  --direction Inbound \
  --access Allow \
  --protocol Tcp \
  --source-address-prefixes 10.0.2.0/24 \
  --source-port-ranges '*' \
  --destination-address-prefixes 10.0.3.0/24 \
  --destination-port-ranges 1433

data.text: **NSGs** provide distributed filtering at the subnet/NIC level. **Azure Firewall** provides centralized logging and outbound control. Together they provide defense in depth: if an NSG rule is misconfigured, the Firewall still protects outbound traffic.
